display.purpose: Archivo 900 at 62% width, uppercase. Giant display words (hero name, contact word, marquee, footer signature, menu links, ghost word, preloader count); aria-hidden when it repeats a heading. Width axis breathes 62-72% with scroll velocity. Archivo is used only at poster scale (2.6rem+): display words, project names, figures, giant numerals.

headline.purpose: Hero H1; carries the accessible meaning of the poster name.

headline-large.purpose: Section headings such as the contact title.

title.purpose: Ticket values and short data headings.

body.purpose: Default reading text; leads capped near 40ch.

nav.purpose: Header links with left-origin underline wipe.

label.purpose: Geist Mono uppercase: corner folios, ticket labels, language switch, browser-bar captions, preloader meta. Never an eyebrow above a heading.

display-name.purpose: Work poster project heading (real h3). Under the hero's 15.5vw so two-word names fit; 17vw on mobile. Breathes; cream swap copy over the screenshot.

display-figure.purpose: Figures plate numbers (real dd values), tabular, count-up; lead figure clamp(7rem, 20vw, 22rem).

display-row.purpose: Archive project names inside the row link.

display-case-name.purpose: Case cover h1, fitted to its longest word via --fit (37/(len x 0.5) vw desktop, --fit-m 88/(len x 0.5) vw mobile, capped 17vw). Next-project name and index title use the same fit with larger caps. Char cascade split as words+chars.

shadows.name: button-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover on orange and cream buttons only.

shadows.name: ticket-drop
shadows.purpose: Boarding ticket; filter so it follows the notched mask.

shadows.name: screen-float
shadows.purpose: Project screens floating inside the gunmetal M window.

shadows.name: object-drop
shadows.purpose: Phase 2 objects on the paper: tools label (0 18px 30px -22px / 0.5), collage cards, capability tickets (0 30px 50px -30px / 0.55), phone (0 30px 40px -20px / 0.6), archive shots (0 30px 50px -25px / 0.55), work browser frame (0 40px 60px -30px / 0.6). Larger object, deeper drop.

shadows.name: cover-drop
shadows.purpose: Deepest object step: case cover frame (0.6) and views desktop frame (0.55). Index card covers 0 24px 40px -24px / 0.55; next-project cover 0 30px 50px -25px / 0.55.

motion.name: ease-out / mc-out
motion.purpose: Entrances: line/char reveals, print-registration, buttons, underline wipes.

motion.name: ease-in-out / mc-inout
motion.purpose: Wipes and portals: M window clip, field, menu clip, preloader scale.

motion.name: ease-soft
motion.purpose: Colour and background transitions.

motion.name: dur-xs
motion.purpose: Opacity micro-states (cursor label).

motion.name: dur-s
motion.purpose: Hover states, label roll, icon rotation.

motion.name: dur-m
motion.purpose: Header hide/show, ticket, menu clip.

motion.name: dur-l
motion.purpose: Section reveals, field scale, image entrances.

motion.name: dur-xl
motion.purpose: Anchor scroll, window inner scale.

motion.name: stamp-spin
motion.purpose: Continuous stamp ring rotation boosted by scroll.

motion.name: breathe-width
motion.purpose: Poster width breathing on data-breathe lines (hero name, work names and swap copies, figures). Shared velocity decays x0.86 per tick once Lenis stops, so width returns to 62% at rest.

motion.name: marquee
motion.purpose: Marquee drift and velocity skew.

motion.name: grain-shift
motion.purpose: Fine grain movement; stops under reduced motion.

motion.name: work-track
motion.value: pinned horizontal translate, scrub 0.6, ease none
motion.purpose: Desktop work track (min-width 861px); prints, phones and tonal numbers trigger via containerAnimation.

motion.name: print-in
motion.value: frame clip inset(0 0 100% 0) -> 0 (1.2s mc-inout); image scale 1.2 -> 1 (1.6s); plates ±16% x / ±5% y -> 0 (1.4s mc-out)
motion.purpose: Imprenta registration on work posters.

motion.name: ticket-stack
motion.value: scale 0.94 (-0.02 per deeper ticket), yPercent -4; content autoAlpha 0, scrubbed
motion.purpose: Covered capability tickets recede leaving edge and numeral.

motion.name: route-draw
motion.value: strokeDashoffset length -> 0, scrub 0.5; stations .is-lit in sequence
motion.purpose: Process route and lit stations.

motion.name: count-up
motion.purpose: Figures plate numbers.

motion.name: depth-scroll
motion.purpose: About collage layers separating with scroll.

motion.name: cursor-float
motion.value: quickTo x/y 0.7s, rotate clamp ±10deg from horizontal speed
motion.purpose: Archive screenshot following the pointer (fine pointers only).

motion.name: plate-wipe
motion.value: ::view-transition-new(root) clip-path inset(100% 0 0 0) -> inset(0), 0.9s cubic-bezier(0.76, 0, 0.24, 1); old root holds
motion.purpose: Cross-document page transition (@view-transition navigation:auto). Header excluded (view-transition-name site-header, no animation). Off under reduced motion; skipped transitions silenced.

motion.name: shared-cover
motion.purpose: Project cover morph between home work poster, index card, case cover and next-project cover. Unique per page.

motion.name: case-intro
motion.value: name chars yPercent 105 -> 0 (1.1s mc-out, stagger 0.03, split words+chars); cover img scale 1.15 -> 1 (1.6s); plates ±16% x / ±5% y -> 0 (1.4s, +0.2s)
motion.purpose: Case cover and index title intro, run in place of the hero intro.

motion.name: built-cascade
motion.value: y 30, autoAlpha 0 -> in, 0.9s mc-out, stagger 0.07, once
motion.purpose: "What we built" list items.

motion.name: views-reveal
motion.value: frame clip inset(0 0 100% 0) -> 0 (1.3s mc-inout); inner image yPercent -6 -> 6 at scale 1.12, scrubbed; phone yPercent 30, rotate 14 -> 0 (1.2s mc-out)
motion.purpose: Case views plate.

motion.name: next-drift
motion.value: next name xPercent 12 -> 0, scrubbed top bottom -> top 30%
motion.purpose: Next-project name drifting into place.

motion.name: index-flip
motion.value: GSAP Flip 0.8s mc-inout, absolute, nested; enter scale 0.92 -> 1 (0.6s mc-out); leave fade to scale 0.92 (0.4s)
motion.purpose: Index filters and Grid/List toggle; instant state change under reduced motion.

motion.name: card-batch
motion.purpose: Index card reveals.

narrative.overview:
The site is a retro-futurist poster series. Every section is a full-bleed plate: a flat field of cream paper, turquoise, orange or gunmetal, with fine animated grain under the content and giant condensed poster lettering that changes colour where it crosses a field. Scrolling turns the pages. The brand M is the recurring device: window, mask, preloader and portal into the next plate.

Two voices carry the type. Archivo, compressed to its narrowest width and set in black uppercase, is the poster: decorative, enormous, often hidden from assistive tech because an accessible Geist heading says the same thing. Geist carries everything that is read, from the H1 down to the button labels, and Geist Mono sets folios, ticket fields and the stamp ring like a printer's slug. Imagery registers like a print run: grayscale source with an orange multiply plate and a deep-turquoise screen plate sliding into register.

Density is low and theatrical at display size, tight and plain at reading size. Ornament is limited to the printer's furniture the world owns natively: rotating circular stamps, ticket stubs, thin orbit lines, four-point stars, registration marks and folios in the margins. Composition is constructivist and flat; depth comes from layering, parallax and colour, never from dimensional type.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed colour plates (cream, turquoise, orange, gunmetal) set by a `data-surface` attribute, each with fine grain under the content.
Archivo 900 at 62% width for poster display only; Geist for everything read.
The brand M as window, mask, preloader and portal.
Printer's furniture as ornament: stamps, ticket stubs, orbits, four-point stars, registration marks, corner folios.
Duotone "print run" imagery with offset colour plates.
Expo-out motion over Lenis smooth scroll, with a full reduced-motion alternative.

Home plate order as built: hero (turquoise/cream) → 02 manifesto (gunmetal) → marquee (orange) → 03 work (gunmetal intro, then orange / turquoise / cream / gunmetal / orange posters) → 04 archive (cream) → 05 capabilities (turquoise) → 06 process (gunmetal) → 07 figures (orange) → 08 about (cream) → 09 contact.

Case page plate order as built: cover (the project's tone) → brief (cream) → what we built (gunmetal) → views (turquoise, or orange when the case tone is turquoise) → CTA (gunmetal) → next project (the next case's tone) → footer. The projects index is one gunmetal plate holding toned project cards.
Pages change like plates: the new page wipes up over the old one, and a project's cover screenshot travels between home poster, index card and case cover.

rules.name: The Gunmetal Reads Rule
rules.body: On orange and turquoise plates, every reading word and every button label is gunmetal (~5.4:1 and ~5.5:1). Cream on orange or turquoise (~2.5:1) and orange on cream (~2.6:1) are allowed only for giant decorative display type marked `aria-hidden`, with the same message present in accessible text nearby. Never use them for body copy, buttons or labels.

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: A section takes one full-bleed field through `data-surface` (cream, turquoise, orange or gunmetal), and that attribute sets both the background and the default text colour. Avoid long, unbroken cream stretches. Alternate plates so orange and turquoise carry the edition.

rules.name: The Colour-Swap Rule
rules.body: Where a poster name crosses an image or a colour field, its letters switch to cream through an `aria-hidden` copy clipped to the crossing area, never by hiding or masking out letters. The hero does it with the M mask (inside the window) and the field clip (over turquoise); the work posters do it with a cream copy clipped to the screenshot rectangle, recomputed on every refresh. The accessible name underneath stays whole.

rules.name: The Project Tone Rule
rules.body: Every project owns one plate tone by its order, in the fixed rotation orange, turquoise, cream, gunmetal, repeating (`projectTone` in src/i18n). The tone follows the project everywhere it appears: home poster, index card, case cover and the next-project plate that points to it. On a gunmetal tone the poster name switches to orange. A case's views plate takes turquoise, or orange when the case itself is turquoise, so two adjacent plates never share a field.

rules.name: The Derived Tones Rule
rules.body: New tints come from `color-mix(in oklab, ...)` between palette colours. No colour from outside the palette enters the system.

rules.name: The Poster-Only Rule
rules.body: Archivo appears only at poster scale, at 62% width, weight 900 and uppercase: giant display words, project names (work poster headings, archive row names, case cover and next-project names, index card and list names), figures, and giant numerals (process stations, capability tickets, work posters). A project name or figure may be the accessible text itself when it is a name or a number, not a sentence. Never use Archivo for running text, buttons, small UI, or anything under 2.6rem. The one sub-scale exception is the type-specimen card in the About collage, which shows the face as a sample inside an `aria-hidden` illustration.

rules.name: The Breathing Width Rule
rules.body: Poster lines marked `data-breathe` (hero name, work project names and their swap copies, figures) widen with scroll velocity, from 62% up to 72% width, then ease back. The shared velocity decays to zero once Lenis stops, so every breathing line returns to 62% at rest. Width is the only axis that breathes. Weight and size stay fixed.

rules.name: The Fitted Poster Name Rule
rules.body: A poster name that has to hold a column is sized to its longest word, never broken mid-word: `font-size: min(role cap, k / (longest word length × 0.5) vw)`, where 0.5 approximates one Archivo character at 62% width in em and k is the width in vw the longest word may take (case cover 37 desktop and 88 mobile, next-project name 52, index title 88). The value is computed at build time into `--fit` (and `--fit-m` for mobile), so a one-word name and a three-word name land at the widest size that keeps every word whole. Single-word display lines that run the full plate use the same idea against their total length (the case CTA word: min(82 / (length × 0.6) vw, 22rem); the contact word, capped at 24rem). Any char cascade on a fitted name splits as words plus chars (`type: 'words,chars'`), so each word stays an unbreakable box when lines are set.

rules.name: The Corner Folio Rule
rules.body: Folios ("02 · MANIFIESTO") live in a corner of the plate (top right, at the gutter) or along the margin, prefixed by a registration-mark glyph drawn in CSS. They are never eyebrows stacked above a heading. Inline mono labels next to data, such as "WhatsApp" before the phone number, are fine.

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: Plates and type never carry shadow, glow or bevel. Only physical objects resting on the paper (tickets, buttons on hover, browser frames, phones, collage cards, paper labels, floating screens) get a soft, negative-spread shadow tinted toward gunmetal.

rules.name: The Covered Ticket Rule
rules.body: In the capability stack, depth is shown by scale, not shadow: as the next ticket slides over, the covered one scales back (about 0.94, less for each deeper ticket), lifts 4%, and fades its title, description and stub, leaving only its edge and giant numeral visible.

rules.name: The Plate Wipe Rule
rules.body: Page changes are cross-document View Transitions (`@view-transition { navigation: auto }`): the new page enters as a plate wiping up from the bottom (clip-path inset(100% 0 0 0) to inset(0), 0.9s on the mc-inout curve) while the old page holds still beneath it. The header is excluded and stays fixed. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` navigation transitions are switched off, and transitions the browser skips (reload, hidden tab) are silenced rather than reported as errors.

rules.name: The Shared Cover Rule
rules.body: Every place a project's cover is shown as the project's primary image carries `view-transition-name: cover-<slug>`: the home work poster frame, the index card cover, the case cover frame, and the next-project cover. A name appears at most once per page, so cursor-follow floats (archive, index list) never carry it, and a case page's own cover and its next-project cover always name different slugs. Between pages, the matching cover morphs on the same 0.9s mc-inout curve as the plate wipe.

dos: Do set every section as a full-bleed plate through `data-surface` (cream, turquoise, orange or gunmetal) with `.grain` under the content.
Do set reading text and button labels in gunmetal on orange and turquoise plates.
Do keep cream-on-orange, cream-on-turquoise and orange-on-cream (~2.5–2.6:1) for giant `aria-hidden` poster display only, with the same message in an accessible Geist heading.
Do use Archivo only at poster scale (2.6rem and up): display words, project names, figures and giant numerals, at weight 900, 62% width, uppercase, line-height 0.78–0.86.
Do switch poster letters to cream where they cross an image or field with a clipped `aria-hidden` copy, keeping the real name whole.
Do pick radii from the scale by object: s for chips and buttons, frame for browser frames and shots, m for tickets and cards, device for phones, arch for the about arch.
Do use Geist for everything read and Geist Mono for folios, data labels and stamp text.
Do place folios in the plate corner (top right at the gutter) or along the margin, with the CSS registration mark.
Do take ornament from the world's own furniture: stamps, ticket stubs, 1–1.5px orbit lines, four-point stars, registration marks, the M silhouette.
Do finish imagery as duotone print plates (orange multiply plus deep-turquoise screen over grayscale).
Do use `mc-out` for entrances and `mc-inout` for wipes and portals, and ship a complete reduced-motion state.
Do give each project its tone by order (orange, turquoise, cream, gunmetal) and carry that tone to every surface that shows the project.
Do fit poster names to their longest word through `--fit`, and split any char cascade on them as words plus chars.
Do put `view-transition-name: cover-<slug>` on every primary appearance of a project's cover, once per page.
Do set `headerOnDark` when a page opens on a dark plate, and point the language switch to the same page in the other locale.
donts: Don't use cream or orange text on colour plates for body copy, buttons, links or labels.
Don't use Archivo for running text, buttons or small UI, or swap Geist for another system face.
Don't hide or mask out letters of a poster name to make it fit over an image; resize the name or swap its colour.
Don't put a folio, kicker or eyebrow label above a heading.
Don't use 3D or extruded type, gradient-filled text, or glow halos around type or UI. Colour light lives only as soft gradients inside a plate's field.
Don't bring in colours from outside the five-colour palette. Derive tints with oklab `color-mix`.
Don't use worn textures, dry brush, speed lines, decorative rays or brush underlines.
Don't put shadows on plates or type. Shadows belong only to objects resting on the paper.
Don't show photos of Mauricio; imagery is the work and surreal, content-tied illustration.
Don't break a poster name mid-word or let a split cascade break it; resize it with the fit instead.
Don't repeat a `cover-<slug>` view-transition name on one page; a duplicate aborts the morph.
